cleanIntro: The Nebula 5.7 is a small can for 5.7x28mm and 22 LR, rated on a 3 inch minimum barrel and full-auto rated in both, with a 90-round limit on sustained full-auto fire before it must cool. It ships on a 1/2-28 direct thread mount that screws into the .900-24 threads of the entrance chamber. Gemtech's routine never opens the can: you take it off the barrel, take the mount off the back of it, clean the thread surfaces, and put it back together dry. Every 600 rounds is Gemtech's minimum for taking it off. Deep Clean is Gemtech's own armorer-level clean, which they call optional but recommended: mount off, the can soaked for an hour in Breakthrough Carbon Pro, and the copper picked out of the blast chamber.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber and action cleared by hand
steps.action: Never take the Nebula off a loaded firearm. Magazine out first, then look into the chamber AND check it with a finger, and clear the action. Gemtech counts a firearm as unloaded only when the action is open, the magazine is out, and you have seen that the chamber is empty.
steps.prose: Your other hand is about to be wrapped around the muzzle end of the gun. Clear it properly before it gets there.
steps.quote: WARNING: NEVER REMOVE A SUPPRESSOR FROM A LOADED FIREARM. FIRST REMOVE THE MAGAZINE FROM THE FIREARM. SECOND, VISUALLY AND MANUALLY CHECK AND CLEAR THE CHAMBER AND ACTION OF AMMUNITION.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Removing Suppressor from the Host Firearm, p.15

steps.title: This book covers the can, not the gun
steps.action: Get your firearm's own manual out and keep it beside this one. Gemtech's book teaches the suppressor — mounting it, cleaning it, its ammunition limits — and sends every firearm procedure back to that firearm's manual.
steps.prose: Two books, two jobs. Anything about clearing, stripping or cleaning the host itself comes from the host's maker.
steps.quote: WARNING: ALWAYS READ AND FOLLOW THE WARNINGS AND INSTRUCTIONS IN THE OWNER’S MANUAL FOR YOUR SPECIFIC FIREARM.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Your Safety Responsibilities, p.4

steps.title: Nothing wider than 5.7mm, and never tracer
steps.action: Before you go any further, check what this can has been fed. Nothing with a bullet wider than 5.7mm, and never tracer. The Nebula 5.7 is rated for 5.7x28mm and 22 Long Rifle, each on a 3 inch minimum barrel.
steps.prose: If you see copper streaks or damage on the end-cap aperture, or hear metal rattling inside, that is a possible baffle strike and the can goes back to Gemtech, not to the bench.
steps.quote: WARNING: DO NOT USE BULLETS WITH A DIAMETER GREATER THAN 5.7MM IN THE NEBULA™ 5.7.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Ammunition Selection, p.10
steps.warn: WARNING: NEVER FIRE “TRACER” AMMUNITION THROUGH YOUR SUPPRESSOR.

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Let the can cool before you take it off. Gemtech puts it past 1000 degrees F in use, and about 10 degrees F hotter for every round fired. If it truly has to come off hot, use a glove or suppressor sock made for extreme heat, and keep it away from anything that can burn.
steps.prose: A hot can does not look hot. Put it somewhere safe to cool before you start.
steps.quote: WARNING: THE SUPPRESSOR CAN BECOME DANGEROUSLY HOT WITH USAGE (> 1000° F) WHICH COULD CAUSE SEVERE SKIN BURNS UPON CONTACT.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Removing Suppressor from the Host Firearm, p.15

steps.title: Can off the barrel, the way the book's removal pages say
steps.action: Gemtech's maintenance section sends you to its own mounting and removal pages for this. The can went on hand tight against the barrel shoulder and was then snugged with a 3/4 inch wrench, so it comes off the reverse way: the wrench on the hex of the mount, counterclockwise, until it breaks free and turns by hand.
steps.prose: Keep the muzzle pointed somewhere safe the whole time you are turning it.
steps.quote: Remove the suppressor from the host firearm by following the instructions listed in the suppressor mounting and removal section of this manual.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance, p.30

steps.title: Mount off the back of the can with a 3/4 inch wrench
steps.action: Put a 3/4 inch wrench on the hex head of the mount at the rear of the can and turn it counterclockwise until the parts break free and can be turned by hand. Then unscrew the mount the rest of the way out of the entrance chamber.
steps.prose: Gemtech's routine clean takes the mount off every time, so its threads and the can's threads can both be cleaned.
steps.quote: Turn the wrench counterclockwise on barrel until the parts are broken free and can be turned by hand.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Mount Removal, p.27

steps.title: Clean it nose-down, and watch the copper
steps.action: Hold the can so loosened debris falls out of it, not into it. Gemtech recommends Breakthrough Carbon Pro for the suppressor, the mount and the accessories, and asks you to watch for copper fouling and not let it build up. Use non-marring tools on the outside so the finish is not damaged.
steps.prose: This is also the moment to look the can, the mount and the barrel threads over for damage or wear.
steps.caution: Use non-marring tools on external surfaces to avoid damaging the finish.
steps.quote: When cleaning, orient the suppressor so that excess debris does not fall into the suppressor.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance, p.30

steps.title: Fouling off every thread surface
steps.action: With the mount out, clean the fouling off its threads and off the threads in the entrance chamber. Carbon Pro and non-marring tools where you need them; nothing abrasive.
steps.prose: Clean, not abrasive. Nothing on this can gets sandpaper or a scouring pad.
steps.caution: However, under NO circumstances should the suppressor’s components be cleaned with an abrasive material such as sand paper, Scotch-Brite®, Crocus Cloth, etc.
steps.quote: Remove the suppressor mount and clean fouling from thread surfaces.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance, p.31

steps.title: Wipe everything dry, threads above all
steps.action: Wipe every surface with a clean rag to get the debris and leftover cleaner off. Every thread has to be clean and dry before anything goes back together.
steps.prose: If any cleaner got inside the can, blow it completely dry with compressed air. Liquid left inside raises the pressure when you fire and can damage the suppressor.
steps.quote: Wipe all surfaces with a clean rag to remove debris and excess cleaning solution.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance, p.31
steps.warn: If any cleaner is introduced to the inside of the suppressor, completely blow dry with a source of compressed air so no residual moisture is left inside.

steps.title: The can stays closed
steps.action: This is where Gemtech's routine stops. Nothing inside the can is yours to adjust or take out — the book gives no procedure for it, and it says not to go past the procedures it prints. Any other service goes to Gemtech.
steps.prose: A damaged tube on a registered suppressor means a new suppressor, not a repair, so do not force anything.
steps.quote: WARNING: NEVER MANIPULATE, ADJUST OR CHANGE ANY OF THE INTERNAL COMPONENTS OF YOUR SUPPRESSOR UNLESS SPECIFICALLY DIRECTED TO DO SO IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Cleaning a Suppressor - General Topics, p.16
steps.warn: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR SUPPRESSOR BEYOND THE PROCEDURES OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the can off the barrel, the mount off the can, and the thread surfaces cleaned and dry. That is all of Gemtech's routine. Deep Clean is their armorer-level clean: the can soaked for an hour and the copper picked out of the blast chamber.
steps.prose: Before it goes back on the gun, check that everything is tight again and that the can is lined up with the bore.
steps.quote: The Nebula™ 5.7 suppressor requires limited maintenance to preserve peak performance.
steps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance, p.30

deepSteps.title: Armorer-level clean: optional, but recommended
deepSteps.action: Gemtech calls this deeper clean optional, but recommended. It is the same whether the can has been shooting 5.7x28mm or 22 LR.
deepSteps.prose: Gemtech suggests doing it once a year, or every 1200 rounds.
deepSteps.aside: This process can be repeated annually, or every 1200 rounds, if desired.
deepSteps.quote: ARMORER LEVEL CLEANING: Deep cleaning of the Nebula™ 5.7 suppressor itself is optional, but recommended.
deepSteps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance - Continued, p.31

deepSteps.title: Thread mount off the can
deepSteps.action: Take the thread mount adapter off the back of the can, the same way as in the routine: 3/4 inch wrench on the hex, counterclockwise until it breaks free, then by hand.
deepSteps.prose: The direct thread mount is one piece; there is nothing further in it to take apart.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the thread mount adapter from the suppressor, and disassemble the mounting system.
deepSteps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance - Continued, p.31

deepSteps.title: Soak the can for one hour, muzzle up
deepSteps.action: Stand the can muzzle up in a container that holds liquid, with the mount beside it. Fill it with Breakthrough Carbon Pro until everything is under, and leave it for one hour.
deepSteps.prose: Do it somewhere with good airflow and wear gloves and eye protection. Gemtech warns that a used suppressor can carry lead residue.
deepSteps.aside: Place the suppressor muzzle up (and its components) in a container that will hold liquid.
deepSteps.quote: Fill container with Breakthrough Clean Technologies® Carbon Pro until the suppressor and components are submerged and let soak for one hour.
deepSteps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance - Continued, p.31

deepSteps.title: Pick the copper out of the blast chamber
deepSteps.action: After the soak, use cleaning picks to get the copper out of the blast chamber, and clean the thread mount as in the routine.
deepSteps.prose: Picks go into the blast chamber only. Nothing further inside the can is yours to work on.
deepSteps.aside: Clean the thread mount following the instructions listed in this manual.
deepSteps.quote: Use cleaning picks to remove copper build up in blast chamber.
deepSteps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance - Continued, p.32

deepSteps.title: Dry it completely
deepSteps.action: Wipe the fouling off the can and the mount and dry them with a cloth, and compressed air if you want. Let everything dry fully before you put it back together.
deepSteps.prose: Liquid left in the can when you fire can damage it.
deepSteps.aside: Allow suppressor and components to dry before reassembly.
deepSteps.quote: Wipe fouling off suppressor and components and dry them using a cloth and compressed air if desired.
deepSteps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Maintenance - Continued, p.32

deepSteps.title: Mount back in: hand tight, then a quarter to a half turn
deepSteps.action: Thread the mount into the base of the entrance chamber by hand until its threads bottom out, without cross-threading and with no power tools. Then put a 3/4 inch wrench on its hex and turn it 1/4 to 1/2 turn clockwise until the parts are snug.
deepSteps.prose: Clean, dry threads before it goes in.
deepSteps.caution: Use a 3/4 inch hex head wrench to engage the mount on the rear of the suppressor and turn 1/4 to 1/2 turn clockwise until the parts are snug.
deepSteps.quote: Thread the mount hand tight into the base of the entrance chamber (FIGURE 2) until the mount’s threads bottom out.
deepSteps.cite: NEBULA 5.7™ SUPPRESSOR SAFETY AND INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV:Gemtech Nebula_5.7_SUPPRESSOR-05-05-2026 — Gemtech Nebula 5.7 Suppressor Mount Installation, p.26

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Interval: off the host every 600 rounds at a minimum
Mount off the can: 3/4 inch wrench on the hex, counterclockwise
Clean fouling from the thread surfaces with Breakthrough Carbon Pro
Hold the can so debris falls out of it, not into it
Watch for copper fouling and do not let it build up
Non-marring tools on the outside, to protect the finish
Do not use abrasives: no sandpaper, Scotch-Brite or crocus cloth

cleaning.name: DRY
tasks: Wipe every surface with a clean rag
All threads clean and dry before reassembly
Any cleaner inside the can: blow it completely dry with compressed air

cleaning.name: BEFORE IT GOES BACK ON
tasks: All mounting parts tight, nothing loosened during cleaning
Alignment checked: nothing in the bore, the muzzle aperture completely circular

reassembly: Let the can and the mount dry fully after the soak before anything goes back together.

Thread the mount into the base of the entrance chamber hand tight until its threads bottom out — no cross-threading, no power tools — then turn it 1/4 to 1/2 turn clockwise with a 3/4 inch hex wrench until snug.
With the firearm unloaded and cleared, take any muzzle device, shim or crush washer off the barrel and clean and degrease the barrel threads with rubbing alcohol.
Screw the can onto the barrel threads hand tight, without cross-threading, until it bottoms out against the barrel shoulder; Gemtech recommends a 3/4 inch wrench to tighten it further.
Confirm every mounting part is tight and nothing loosened during maintenance, then confirm alignment before firing.
fncheck: With the firearm unloaded and cleared, check the can is mounted straight to the centreline of the bore, then look through the chamber to the muzzle: nothing may block the bullet's path and the muzzle aperture must look completely circular. Shadows or half-moons mean the can must be realigned before it is fired; Gemtech also recommends a suppressor alignment gauge. While shooting, check regularly, after letting it cool, that it is still tight — Gemtech says every direct thread mounted suppressor will loosen with use.
